shared_elements: upright monolithic stone slab/pillar carved in low relief
central circular disc motif on the broad face
paired symmetrical curved/arched elements above the disc
horizontal band or belt-like register crossing the body
narrower upper block with its own set of vertical motifs
justification: Both are tall monoliths worked in shallow relief with a comparable vertical scheme: a narrower upper block carrying its own motifs, then a broad face where paired symmetrical curved elements sit above a prominent central disc, with a horizontal band or belt below. The decisive difference is content and handling: A's relief is crisply linear and unmistakably zoomorphic (profile quadrupeds, long-necked birds, a zigzag frieze), while B's motifs are broad, rounded and largely abstract/anthropomorphic on a dark, coarse stone, so no shared hand or repertoire can be argued.
